regressions.summary: A privacy acknowledgement retained for human handoff was also projected as a reusable answer question.

candidates.failure_pattern: A shared workflow record feeds multiple projections whose semantic classification is reconstructed independently by consumers.
candidates.cause: The review record preserves a human-only item without carrying a canonical projection classification, so the answer-queue consumer must infer whether it is reusable from the prompt text.

detection_signal.description: Exercise the same review record through the handoff-only and answerable projections, asserting that only the answerable question reaches the reusable queue.

likely_false_positives: A projection intentionally owns a distinct semantic classification documented at its producer-consumer boundary.
A record is display-only and never feeds a reusable or automated downstream consumer.
candidates.remediation: Persist the semantic classification on the shared workflow record and require each projection to consume that canonical field; until then, keep the repository-owned conservative classifier and regression proof.

transitions.reason: The confirmed defect received an isolated repository regression proof.
The defect instantiates a broader producer-consumer classification boundary that may repeat across repositories.
The originating repository is protected, but independent fleet precision and cost evidence do not yet support required enforcement.
